boards.title: What the Campus Tour Skips: 10 Places Students Share With Each Other
boards.description: Ten named McNichols Campus places documented by Detroit Mercy as student meeting, study, recreation, reflection, or gathering spaces.

cards.title: McNichols Campus Library
cards.subtitle: McNichols Campus — between Architecture and Chemistry
cards.notes: Set up in the stacks or quiet-study areas for focused work, then use the library’s research and circulation desks when you need support.
cards.short_summary: A separate campus library building with quiet study areas and research help.
cards.evidence_claim: Detroit Mercy lists the Library’s stacks and quiet study rooms as informal student study spaces and identifies the building’s McNichols Campus location.
cards.access_notes: Check the library’s current hours before visiting.

cards.title: Student Union
cards.subtitle: McNichols Campus
cards.notes: Meet classmates around the building’s shared tables, then choose a breakout room when your conversation needs a more focused setup.
cards.short_summary: A central campus hub with study, social, dining, and student-service spaces.
cards.evidence_claim: Detroit Mercy says the Student Union has breakout rooms for studying and socializing, plus ping-pong and pool tables.
cards.access_notes: Some rooms and services may have separate access or reservation requirements.

cards.title: Fountain Lounge
cards.subtitle: Student Union, first floor
cards.notes: Use the soft seating for a low-key meet-up or independent work session; keep an eye out for scheduled events that may change the setup.
cards.short_summary: An adaptable first-floor lounge beside the Student Union fountain patio.
cards.evidence_claim: Detroit Mercy identifies Fountain Lounge as a first-floor Student Union space with soft seating and notes that it hosts various events.
cards.access_notes: Soft seating must remain in the lounge; event use can affect availability.

cards.title: Quad Commons
cards.subtitle: Center of the Quads
cards.notes: Bring a laptop to the first-floor lounge or meet a small group here; the basement adds additional rooms to the commons.
cards.short_summary: A residence-area commons used for hanging out, studying, and group meetings.
cards.evidence_claim: Detroit Mercy describes Quad Commons as a hangout and study spot where campus groups also hold meetings.
cards.access_notes: Located in the residential Quads area; observe residence-hall access rules.

cards.title: Quad Commons Theater
cards.subtitle: Quad Commons, basement floor
cards.notes: Plan a student-organization meeting or movie night in the theater, using the television when the room is available to your group.
cards.short_summary: A basement theater designed for relaxed group meetings and movie nights.
cards.evidence_claim: Detroit Mercy states that the Quad Commons Theater can be used by student organizations or groups to meet, relax, and host movie nights.
cards.access_notes: Located in a residential commons; confirm availability and applicable access rules.

cards.entity_name: Michael & Gail Whitty Student Fitness Center
cards.title: Whitty Student Fitness Center
cards.subtitle: McNichols Campus
cards.notes: Activate your Detroit Mercy ID at the front desk, then use the courts, fitness equipment, study areas, or included fitness classes.
cards.short_summary: A student fitness and recreation building with courts, equipment, and study areas.
cards.evidence_claim: Detroit Mercy says current students receive free membership and lists free fitness classes, court reservations, equipment access, and an excellent place to study.
cards.source_title: Get Started | University of Detroit Mercy Recreation
cards.access_notes: Detroit Mercy ID activation is required; the university lists hours as Monday–Thursday, 11 a.m.–8 p.m., subject to change.

cards.title: Architecture Pit
cards.subtitle: Architecture building, McNichols Campus
cards.notes: Use this named interior study area for a change of scenery, especially when you need to spread out with classmates between classes.
cards.short_summary: A named informal study space in the Architecture building.
cards.evidence_claim: Detroit Mercy’s McNichols student-space guide lists the Architecture Pit among informal indoor student spaces.
cards.access_notes: Observe building access policies and avoid disrupting scheduled academic activity.

cards.title: St. Ignatius Chapel
cards.subtitle: Commerce & Finance building, first floor
cards.notes: Stop in for a quiet moment of reflection, or attend a scheduled service if it fits your day; respect worship and event use.
cards.short_summary: A small first-floor chapel on the McNichols Campus.
cards.evidence_claim: Detroit Mercy describes St. Ignatius Chapel as a small church on the first floor of the Commerce & Finance building with a piano.
cards.access_notes: Use respectfully and defer to posted worship, event, and building-access guidance.

cards.title: Fisher Fountain
cards.subtitle: South side of the McNichols Campus Library
cards.notes: Take a study break at the outdoor fountain area, using the benches for a conversation or a few quiet minutes between campus stops.
cards.short_summary: An outdoor fountain immediately south of the McNichols Campus Library.
cards.evidence_claim: Detroit Mercy’s library location page states that Fisher Fountain is on the south side of the McNichols Campus Library.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor conditions and campus programming can affect comfort and availability.

cards.title: Shiple Hall First Floor Lounge
cards.subtitle: Shiple Hall, first floor
cards.notes: Use the first-floor lounge to meet residents or settle into a casual study session, while keeping noise and traffic considerate of hall life.
cards.short_summary: A listed residential-area lounge for informal student use.
cards.evidence_claim: Detroit Mercy’s McNichols student-space guide lists the Shiple first-floor lounge as an informal indoor student space.
cards.access_notes: This is in a residence hall; follow residence-hall guest and access policies.
